prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one polished art-direction contact sheet for the B03 Pumpkin Cemetery Town game region. This is an illustrated concept board, not an exact-coordinate floorplan.
Input image 1 is ONLY the approved rendering-style reference: match its bright painted fantasy look, high three-quarter near-isometric camera, clean illustrated outlines, strong 2.5D volumes, sunny material detail and fresh colors. Do not reuse its UI, bronze industrial winches, ruins or monsters.
Create a high-resolution wide landscape sheet, preferably 3840 x 1920, with EXACTLY four columns and two rows of equally sized panels: seven distinct complete room environments and an eighth isolated prop showcase. Each scene is an independent place with its own layout and architecture, NOT crops or slices of one large map. All seven panels have the same camera angle and scale. Thin cream parchment gutters and small brass-edged cream ID tabs. The only written text is the exact panel IDs.
Overall world: cheerful living cartoon undead village in warm midday sunshine. Mint-green plaster, lavender tiled roofs, cream stone paving, orange pumpkins, lilac patchwork cloth, polished mint-colored brass buckles, round white flowers and green foliage. Sunny fantasy 2.5D hand-painted game art, humorous undead daily life, expressive intact pale-mint zombies, no gore. Fun impossible elements such as yawning coffin post offices, hats on headstones, ghost tea servers, moon sails, autonomous spoons and flower candles. Material texture is crisp and controlled, not muddy or photorealistic.
Every room has a large continuous traversable pale stone/wood center and generous connected paths. Rich varied props and full buildings stay mainly on the outer streets and natural edges. Three small auto-buff beacon pedestals and two or three visibly distinct grave-seal lamps can be illustrated around the sides. Buildings are complete designed volumetric objects; no flat texture extruded into a tall wall. Edge paving blends gradually with grass, flower beds and village roads; the environment continues beyond the arena without a hard rectangle or grey border. Do not clutter combat centers with piles of props.

Panel layout in reading order:
Top-left, exact ID "L13": Pumpkin Gate Street. A sleepy yawning coffin-shaped POST OFFICE landmark at upper-left, mint-and-lavender cottages at far edges, a wide gently bent welcome street through the center with a short rear-street connection. Cat-shaped direction signs, hat headstones, a pumpkin flower cart, small ghost tea stall, tiny coffin mailboxes, patchwork awning and invitation notice board. Orange pumpkin flowers grow into the natural lane edges. Show one small lantern-sentry zombie and one shovel zombie at believable game scale.

Top-second, exact ID "L14": Sunlit Candy Warehouse. A round pumpkin-shaped translucent candy WAREHOUSE with candy-paper windows at upper-right, bright open street running diagonally from lower-left to upper-right, a separate narrow back-street shortcut but no high shelves blocking the center. Clear star-candy crates, stacked glass candy jars wearing hats, patchwork candy sacks, a small pumpkin sugar kettle, candy-paper arch and short candy-drying stand. Open airy sugar trade village, not factory pipes. Two small complete cartoon zombies: crossbow operator and candy-pot carrier.

Top-third, exact ID "L15": Grave-Bell Plaza. A beautiful three-petal HAT-ROOF BELL PAVILION at upper edge, broad open cream circular-town plaza with a low pumpkin sundial and an open southern ring lane. Hat headstones act like a whimsical audience, a tea stall, paper flower cart, pumpkin balloon garland and low curved flower beds. Copper hat chimes and ribbons are playful, not spooky. Small hopping zombie and ring-bearing conductor on opposite sides. No grid of collision blocks in the plaza.

Top-right, exact ID "L16": Candle-Oven Street. A distinctive TWO-OVEN PUMPKIN CANDLE BAKERY at upper-right: one smiling orange oven makes candy, one lilac hat oven makes candle flowers. Two wide connected streets across the middle, distinguished by paving details rather than walls. White candle blossoms on little trees, candy hanging on short drying racks, tiny flower-wax barrels, purple cat-tail wick spools, patchwork awnings and warm shop windows. A candy-pot zombie and cold-mist backpack zombie stay away from the open center. Daylight remains dominant; small stable candle flames.

Bottom-left, exact ID "L17": Patchwork Workshop. A fanciful OPEN TOP-HAT TAILOR SHOP landmark on the upper-left edge, with a sewing-needle sign and patchwork roof. Central work street entirely open, a southern side lane connects the goals. A few small colorful spool tables, padded doll dress forms, thread-and-shuttle arch, orange/lavender/mint cloth banners, flowering giant cloth-thread spool and ghost lunch tea stall. A scissors-tailor zombie and coffin-shield zombie. The spools are fabric, never electrical coils or industrial winches.

Bottom-second, exact ID "L18": Ghost-Lantern Pier. A continuous bright wood-and-stone waterfront street through the center, village cottages at top, a curved natural shoreline only at the lower OUTSIDE edge, with mint water and white flowering lily pads beyond it. A large whimsical MOON-SAIL FERRY at lower-right edge has a top-hat cabin, mint hull and pumpkin lantern chain. Small sleepy ghost pumpkin boats, a tiny pumpkin mooring bollard, seashell buoy, hat-wearing singing conch, dream-ticket coffin mailbox and tea stall. Water must not intrude into the arena as any rectangular pool or pit. Two or three small village undead at proper game scale.

Bottom-third, exact ID "BO03": Mayor Boss Courtyard. Wide bright town-festival cemetery plaza with a completely open central arena. A lavender hat-roof TOWN HALL sits on upper-right edge and a low patchwork festival theatre at upper-left. Hat audience headstones, pumpkin flower beds, a top-hat carriage, unmailed invitation box, brass chimes and a thread arch frame the outskirts. At center is the STITCHED MAYOR: a large friendly-menacing intact mint zombie with tall crooked top hat, warm patchwork coat, pumpkin lantern cane and bright stitching. Three grave counter-lamps around the sides. One tasteful thin curved thread attack cue and one tiny pumpkin barrel illustrate his character; keep floor readable and no giant attack overlays.

Bottom-right, exact ID "PROPS": A cream parchment illustrated prop collection showing a coffin mailbox, hat headstone, pumpkin flowercart, ghost tea server, rotating hat chime, star-candy crate, flower candle tree, smiling pumpkin sugar pot, fabric spool table, padded doll, moon-sail boat and mint-brass pumpkin grave lamp. Each is a gorgeous separate 2.5D object with consistent directional sunlight and neat shadows; no written descriptions.

Constraints: all eight IDs correctly spelled, no other text, no HUD, no logos, no watermarks, no black void around rooms, no dark cemetery treatment, no blood, no corpses, no skeleton piles, no rusted industrial tools, no steam winches, no electrical wire coils, no giant rectangular water pools/pits, no raised rectangular terrain slabs, no high stretched floor-texture walls, no rigid tiled asset repetition, no obstructed combat centers, no dramatic night lighting, no giant blurry foreground leaves. The finished sheet should feel like an attractive premium playable fantasy village game with seven clearly distinct spaces.
